one_liner: Sandboxed RISC-V (RV32EM/RV64EM) VM with a single-pass x86-64 recompiler: compiles 170-470x faster than Wasmtime Cranelift, executes near Wasmtime speed.
what_it_does: PolkaVM runs untrusted guest programs compiled for its own RISC-V-derived ISA (no floating point, no SIMD) inside a sandbox, with optional synchronous or asynchronous gas metering. Guests are built with Rust and linked into a .polkavm blob by polkatool; the host embeds the polkavm crate (Engine, Module, Linker, Instance) and calls exported functions. It is not a WebAssembly runtime, so adopting it means retargeting guest code, not swapping an engine.
how_it_is_fast: The recompiler translates RISC-V instructions to x86-64 in a single O(n) pass with its own assembler, which is why compile time is in microseconds where Cranelift's optimising pipeline takes tens of milliseconds. Despite the single pass, its output is only about 11% slower than Cranelift's on pinky and about equal on prime-sieve. Compiler scratch buffers are reused across compilations, and the Engine keeps a pool of pre-spawned sandbox worker processes (default 2) so instantiation does not fork a process.
when_to_use: Hosts that load many different untrusted programs and run each briefly, where compile latency dominates: blockchain smart contracts (Polkadot SDK's pallet-revive and sc-executor-polkavm depend on it) or plugin systems.
x86-64 Linux deployments that need deterministic execution plus built-in gas metering; async gas costs about 14% on pinky execution vs 44% for Wasmtime fuel metering (derived from page data).

Workloads of a few hundred milliseconds of guest execution or less: on pinky the 62 ms Cranelift compile only pays for itself after about 96 emulated frames (about 0.6 s of execution, derived from page data).
When you control the guest toolchain (Rust, or C via the guest header in capi/) and can target its RISC-V ISA instead of Wasm.
when_not_to_use: Existing WebAssembly modules or a Wasm toolchain you cannot change: there is no Wasm front end (issue #37 is still research).

Long-running or call-heavy guests: steady-state execution is equal to or slower than Wasmtime Cranelift (pinky 6.422 ms vs 5.776 ms) and the recompiler's per-call cost is 4.852 us vs 0.252 us for Wasmtime on the minimal program (about 19x).
Tiny programs: PolkaVM's own interpreter does the minimal one-shot in 2.533 us vs 113.743 us for its recompiler, and Wasmi in about 26 us.

Non-x86-64 or non-Linux hosts: the recompiler is compiled only for x86-64 Linux (macOS/FreeBSD x86-64 behind the experimental generic-sandbox feature); aarch64 and everything else fall back to the interpreter, which is about 30x slower on pinky.
Floating-point or SIMD guest code, a C host API (issue #132 open), or production stability: the README says unfinished, heavy work in progress, do not use in production.

integration.dependencies: log, picosimd, polkavm-assembler, polkavm-common (all in-repo except log and picosimd); polkavm-linux-raw on x86-64 Linux; optional schnellru for module-cache; guests need polkatool and a nightly Rust for -Z build-std
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.86.0 (crate 0.37.0); benchmarked commit used Rust 1.82.0 for the host and nightly-2024-11-01 for guests
integration.platforms: Recompiler: x86-64 Linux (x86-64 macOS/FreeBSD only with the experimental generic-sandbox feature); interpreter everywhere, including no_std
integration.thread_safety: not documented in the files read

gotchas: Harness note (no bug found behind the numbers): 'one-shot' starts the timer after Engine creation, and PolkaVM's Engine::new pre-spawns two Linux sandbox worker processes that are reused between instantiations, so cold process start is excluded (Wasmtime's Engine creation is excluded too). Even so, on the minimal program about 107 us of PolkaVM's 113.7 us one-shot is instantiation beyond compile and run (derived from page data).

Harness note: Wasm guests were built with -C target-cpu=mvp -C target-feature=-sign-ext, i.e. without bulk-memory or sign-extension ops, while the headline PolkaVM row is the 64-bit RV64EMAC build; benchtool at HEAD still pins Wasmtime 26.0.1 and Wasmer 5.0.0 and BENCHMARKS.md has not been regenerated since 2024-11-24 (crate now 0.37.0). Only prime-sieve validates its output (asserts in initialize); pinky's timed path has no output check.

Open correctness issue #413 (2026-08-15): interpreter and recompiler disagree on memset operand width (interpreter truncates dst and count to 32 bits) in the Latest32/Latest64 instruction sets, so crosscheck runs can diverge; #402 (Linux sandbox rewrite, correctness and performance, P-high) is pending.
Gas metering variants are not free: sync gas adds about 24% to pinky execution and 81% to prime-sieve one-shot on the 64-bit recompiler (derived from page data).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick PolkaVM over Wasmi, wasm3 or DLR-FT's interpreter when guests do real work: on pinky its recompiler executes about 17x faster than Wasmi (6.4 ms vs 112 ms) while compiling in 0.17 ms; pick it over wisp, zwasm or Wasmtime Winch when you can leave Wasm and want both microsecond compile and near-Cranelift execution, and stay with Wasmi or PolkaVM's interpreter for tiny, call-once programs.
verified_claims_summary: The author's benchtool (criterion, sample size 10, Threadripper 3970X, turbo off, pinned to two cores, commit 190ea5ac, 2024-11-24) shows PolkaVM's 64-bit recompiler finishing compile+instantiate+run in 55.4 ms on the pinky NES emulator vs 116.0 ms for Wasmtime 26 Cranelift and 137.8 ms for Wasmer 5 singlepass, and 14.4 ms vs 125.1 ms on prime-sieve; the win comes from compile time (0.168 ms vs 62.2 ms on pinky), while steady-state execution is at parity or slower.
status_note: Very active (crate 0.37.0 released 2026-09-28, about 9.75M crates.io downloads, last commit 2026-10-06) and MIT OR Apache-2.0, used by Polkadot SDK crates despite the README's not-for-production warning; the benchmark is first-party and two years old, and the enricher found no correctness bug behind the measured numbers.
